title: Your Saturday Night on Really TV: From Salvage Hunts to Haunted Houses
excerpt: A no‑frills rundown of what to stream on Really TV this weekend, with sharp takes on the big‑ticket shows and tailored picks for every mood and age group.
content:
If you’re looking for something to keep you glued to the screen this weekend, Really TV has pulled together a mix of nostalgia, curiosity and a touch of the supernatural. Here’s a breakdown of the main events and a few recommendations for the different groups in your household.

Salvage Hunters – the Bounty‑Hunter Series That Keeps On Giving

Starting early at 05:00 GMT, the first episode of Season 18 sees Drew and Viki on the hunt for a Georgian bookcase and a 19th‑century carved deer. Their knack for spotting hidden value makes the show a reliable source of fresh, visual intrigue. If you enjoy the thrill of discovery and the satisfaction of a good bargain, this is the one to start your evening with.

Celebrity Fantasy Homes – Luxe Real Estate with a Twist

At 06:00 GMT, Gaby Roslin teams up with former footballer Lee Sharpe to find a dream property on the Costa del Sol. The 400,000‑pound budget keeps the stakes moderate, but the show’s polished presentation makes for a nice, relaxed viewing experience. Ideal for adults who appreciate a touch of glamour without the drama.

Cruise TV with LoveitBookit – Your Virtual Pass to the High Seas

At 07:00 GMT, the channel offers a one‑hour cruise guide. It’s a light, scenic break that’s perfect for anyone who wants to escape the dreariness of a rainy evening. The segment’s “ground‑breaking ships” focus keeps it fresh for repeat viewers.

The Repair Shop – Hand‑Crafted Nostalgia

From 12:00 to 18:00 GMT, the series returns with a line‑up of restoration projects – from speedway boots to a 1960s electric organ. Each episode is a gentle reminder that craftsmanship still matters. Perfect for families with older children who appreciate a craft‑based narrative.

Ghost Adventures – A Slightly Creepy Option

After the Repair Shop, the channel switches to the paranormal with “Possession In Pilot Rock” at 21:00 GMT. While it may be a tad spooky, the show’s investigative style holds up well for viewers who like a bit of mystery without the fear factor.

Help! My House Is Haunted – The Ultimate Haunted House Marathon

Starting at 23:00 GMT, a full‑night run of the series takes you through Chillingham Castle, the Leopard Inn, and more. The show’s blend of history and modern investigation offers a compelling scroll‑through for those who enjoy the supernatural with a documentary edge.

The Hotel Inspector – A Renovation Reality Show

After midnight, Alex Polizzi returns to Michelangelo’s near Newcastle. The episode’s focus on a 10‑bedroom hotel combined with A‑list business advice keeps the pace brisk and the tone uplifting. Great for adults who appreciate a mix of hospitality and actionable insight.

My Lottery Dream Home – The Lottery‑Backed House Hunt

Beginning at 14:00 GMT, David Bromstad helps lucky winners find dream homes across the US. The series offers a mixture of design and real‑world budgeting that can appeal to anyone with a dream of property ownership.

A Place In The Sun – British Couples Seek Sunshine

At 17:00 GMT, several episodes follow British couples as they trade grey skies for sun. The show’s steady pacing and supportive tone make it a reliable pick for families who love travel and home‑shopping.

Long Lost Family: What Happened Next – Emotional Family Reunions

At 21:00 GMT, the show revisits families re‑united by Davina McCall and Nicky Campbell. The emotional depth and narrative clarity make it a valuable watch for older viewers seeking heart‑warming content.

Who Do You Think You Are? – A Genealogical Deep Dive

At 22:00 GMT, Twiggy’s story unravels the mystery of her family’s past. The show’s intimate approach and expert storytelling make it a solid choice for viewers interested in personal history.

Bottom line: Whether you’re a bargain hunter, a design enthusiast, a paranormal aficionado, or just looking for a comforting family drama, Really TV’s lineup this weekend offers something that fits your mood. Pick a niche, switch it on, and enjoy a relaxed, well‑curated evening.
